title: Show HN: Neural Particle Automata
summary: Neural Particle Automata extends grid-based Neural Cellular Automata to free-moving agentic particles that can change state and position while following simple shared rules, enabling complex self-organizing patterns and regenerative capabilities demonstrated by a lizard that heals itself when cut.
problem_solved: Removes the grid constraint from cellular automata, allowing for more flexible self-organizing systems where particles can move freely and still maintain emergent pattern formation and regeneration.
why_valuable: It demonstrates how simple local rules can produce complex self-healing and morphogenetic behaviors in free-moving particle systems, advancing our understanding of emergence and self-organization with potential applications in robotics, synthetic biology, and tissue engineering.
